newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil approves initial block sale of CVRD.
newsitem.headline: Brazil approves initial block sale of CVRD.

text.p: Brazil's National Privatization Council Thursday approved an initial block sale of 40-45 percent of voting shares in the sell-off of state mining conglomerate Companhia Vale do Rio Doce, an official said.
The head of the BNDES development bank, Luiz Carlos Mendonca de Barros, said the privatization would begin in February 1997 with the block sale.
Immediately after the block sale, 10 percent of CVRD's total capital will be offered to staff, Mendonca de Barros told reporters.
He said a public offering on international and domestic markets would follow from June 1997 on.
The government owns 76 percent of CVRD's voting capital, equivalent to 51 percent of the company's total capital.

Mendonca de Barros said Brazil's privatization council had approved several rules which sought to restrict the takeover of CVRD by major producers, consumers and traders of iron ore and avoid "volatility" in its control following privatization.

Under the rules for the auction of the 40-45 percent block share, iron ore producers of over 30 million tonnes a year, consumers of over 8.0 million tonnes annually and traders of over 30 million tonnes a year of iron ore will be restricted to a maximum of 45 percent of the block sale.

Mendonca de Barros said existing minority shareholders would have the right to offer their shares for sale along with the auction of Valecom or may associate themselves with the new holding after privatization.

The government will maintain two "golden shares", one in Valecom to ensure its rules are observed for five years, the other a permanent veto over changes in CVRD's iron ore, railway and ports business interests, as well changes in the company's name and the location of its headquarters.

Mendonca de Barros said, given the size and complexity of the CVRD sell-off, plus the possible impact of a bill currently in Congress to cut taxes on exports, the minimum price of shares will be decided 60 days before the block sale.
Separate minimum prices will be decided later for sales to staff and the national and international public offerings.
The government was also considering the use by staff of FGTS funds. The FGTS or Time Served Guarantee Fund is a fund set up to guarantee compensation to workers in case of dismissal.
